item.title: Configure External Authentication
item.description: KubeSphere Enterprise supports configuring external authentication. Platform administrators can configure identity providers through Secrets. After configuring an external identity provider, users can log in to the KubeSphere Enterprise web console using their LDAP, CAS, GitHub, Alibaba Cloud IDaaS, or OpenID Connect username and password. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere Enterprise web console with a user having the platform-admin role. Click Cluster Management and enter the host cluster.

item.title: LDAP/LDAPS Authentication
item.description: KubeSphere supports external authentication through LDAP and LDAPS, allowing users to log in to the KubeSphere Enterprise web console using their LDAP or LDAPS username and password. Platform administrators can configure LDAP/LDAPS authentication through Secrets. LDAP vs LDAPS Authentication Method Connection Method Security LDAP Plain text transmission, default port 389 Data transmission is not encrypted, not suitable for production environments.

item.title: OIDC Authentication
item.description: KubeSphere supports external authentication through OpenID Connect (OIDC), allowing users to log in to the KubeSphere Enterprise web console using their OIDC username and password. Platform administrators can configure OIDC authentication through Secrets. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere Enterprise web console with a user having the platform-admin role. Click Cluster Management and enter the host cluster. Click Configuration > Secrets in the left navigation pane.
